title: FYP: Traffic Choking Point Detector
summary: Final Year Project (BS Computer Science, NUML). A CCTV-based system that detects vehicles, NUML buses, pedestrians and traffic controllers at two Islamabad locations, tracks them with ByteTrack, and raises SMS and dashboard alerts when counts exceed a congestion threshold. YOLOv8n reached 89.5% validation and 89.1% held-out test mAP@50.
role: Lead AI Engineer (Final Year Project). Responsible for the complete AI lifecycle: dataset annotation, YOLOv8 fine-tuning, ByteTrack integration, and connecting the AI pipeline with the full-stack web application.
problem: Traffic near the NUML campus, especially at 7-Up Chowk and the NUML gate, is monitored through manual observation, radio calls and phone calls, so interventions are slow. Existing CCTV cameras mostly act as passive recorders.
solution: A fine-tuned YOLOv8n model detects four classes (vehicle, Numl_Bus, Human, Controller) on live CCTV frames. ByteTrack assigns persistent IDs to prevent double counting. Congestion is flagged when vehicle and bus counts exceed a threshold, crowd density is checked against a human-count limit, and the system checks whether a traffic controller is present before alerting.
architecture: 1. CCTV/IP stream capture (OpenCV, auto-reconnect) -> 2. YOLOv8n detection -> 3. ByteTrack + Supervision tracking -> 4. Threshold-based congestion, crowd and controller-presence logic -> 5. FastAPI backend (WebSocket) with SQLite logging -> 6. SMS/email and dashboard alerts on a React admin dashboard with JWT login and admin approval.
results: Validation results: 89.5% mAP@50, 59.3% mAP@50–95, 86.4% precision, and 84.7% recall. On a held-out test split of 162 images and 799 instances: 89.1% mAP@50, 54.8% mAP@50–95, 82.2% precision, and 86.8% recall. Test mAP@50 by class: NUML bus 95.9%, controller 94.2%, vehicle 89.7%, and human 76.6%. Inference measured 3.1–5.7 ms per image on a Tesla T4. The model was trained for 282 epochs; the best checkpoint was epoch 232.
challenges: Error analysis showed background false positives, particularly for the human and vehicle classes. Human detection was the weakest class on the held-out test set at 76.6% mAP@50.
limitations: Two fixed locations only. Congestion is a count threshold, not a learned model. Accuracy drops in fog, glare and night conditions. User testing was small. No evaluation yet on unseen cameras.
nextSteps: Re-evaluate with a split by video, error-analyse the Human class, benchmark optimized inference latency, and evaluate congestion alerts against human-labelled states.

title: Podcaster Crew: Multi-Agent Automated Research-to-Podcast & Audio Engine
summary: Autonomous multi-agent system built with CrewAI that automates the end-to-end research-to-podcast pipeline: research gathering, markdown reporting, two-host natural dialogue script generation, and Gemini TTS voice synthesis.
problem: Creating high-quality topical podcasts or technical audio digests requires hours of manual literature review, syntheses of recent developments, scripting entertaining two-host conversational banter with audio cues, and manual voiceover recording.
solution: Built Podcaster Crew, a sequential multi-agent architecture where a 'Researcher' agent conducts real-time web retrieval on any topic, a 'Reporting Analyst' synthesizes insights into structured markdown, a 'Scriptwriter' crafts an engaging two-host dialogue with humor and narration pauses, and a voice synthesis module produces ready-to-publish MP3 audio with Gemini TTS.
architecture: Topic Input -> Researcher Agent (Serper Search & News Ingestion) -> Reporting Analyst (Synthesis & Markdown Structuring) -> Scriptwriter Agent (Natural Two-Host Dialogue & Audio FX Cues) -> Gemini TTS Pipeline -> Generated MP3 Audio Output.
results: Automates complete podcast production from topic prompt to multi-voice audio within minutes. Modular design allows dynamic topic switching (AI trends, healthcare, space tech) without altering agent topologies.
challenges: Generating realistic conversational rhythm and avoiding sterile monologues. Solved by designing explicit conversational persona prompts with turn-taking logic, natural pauses, and TTS voice persona mapping.

title: DiaBp Diet Consultant: AI-Powered RAG Health Assistant & Medical OCR App
summary: RAG-powered health assistant for diabetes and hypertension that provides personalized diet plans grounded in medical literature and extracts information from uploaded medical documents with OCR.
problem: Patients with chronic conditions (Type 2 Diabetes and Hypertension) struggle to decipher clinical lab reports and translate medical dietary guidelines into daily, personalized meal plans tailored to their specific biometrics and medications.
solution: Built a RAG-powered assistant for diabetes and hypertension with personalized multi-week diet plans, medical-document OCR, authentication, health tracking, and an admin dashboard. The project includes a Flutter mobile app and a Next.js web application with a FastAPI backend.
architecture: Flutter and Next.js clients -> FastAPI -> Sentence Transformers and FAISS retrieval over medical literature -> Gemini response generation; OCR extracts information from uploaded medical documents.
results: Grounds diet-plan generation in medical literature. Formal groundedness and hallucination evaluation against a no-retrieval baseline is in progress.
challenges: Evaluating how reliably retrieval grounds generated nutrition recommendations is an open task; a formal comparison against a no-retrieval baseline is in progress.

title: DiaBP Diet Consultant: AI-Powered Full-Stack Web Platform (RAG & FastAPI)
summary: Full-stack Next.js & FastAPI web platform generating personalized medical diet plans (1 week to 1 month) for diabetes and hypertension patients using Google Gemini, FAISS vector RAG, Tesseract OCR document parsing, and real-time WebSockets.
problem: Patients managing chronic diabetes and hypertension require continuous, personalized dietary guidance grounded in verified medical literature, along with the ability to ingest physical lab reports and export structured multi-week meal plans in professional formats.
solution: Engineered DiaBP Diet Consultant Web App, a complete production web platform combining Next.js with FastAPI. Integrates an AI RAG pipeline with FAISS vector search over medical guidelines, Google Gemini for context-aware diet generation, Tesseract OCR for physical document parsing, real-time WebSocket communication, and client-side jsPDF diet plan downloads.
architecture: Next.js Web Client -> WebSocket / REST API -> FastAPI Backend (SQLAlchemy / SQLite) -> Tesseract OCR & PyMuPDF (Lab Report Extraction) -> FAISS Vector Store (Medical Guidelines via Sentence Transformers) -> Google Gemini LLM (Context-Aware Synthesis) -> jsPDF Meal Plan Export & Admin Analytics.
results: Delivered end-to-end multi-duration diet plans (1 week, 10 days, 2 weeks, 3 weeks, 1 month) customized to patient biometrics, blood pressure, glucose, and HbA1c. Features comprehensive patient tracking, BMI classification, and admin health analytics dashboards.
challenges: Grounding personalized diet guidance in medical literature while processing uploaded documents. Formal groundedness and hallucination evaluation against a no-retrieval baseline is in progress.

title: Sales Demand Forecasting with XGBoost & Time-Series Engineering
summary: End-to-end predictive analytics pipeline utilizing XGBoost gradient boosting and advanced time-series feature engineering to forecast retail product demand and optimize supply chain inventory.
problem: Retail supply chains suffer substantial losses from stockouts during demand spikes or capital lockup from excess inventory due to traditional moving-average forecasts failing to capture nonlinear seasonal trends and lagged effects.
solution: Developed a time-series forecasting pipeline using XGBoost. Engineered comprehensive temporal features (cyclical day-of-week, month encoding, holiday flags) and autoregressive lag indicators (t-1, t-7, rolling 14-day window statistics) to accurately model complex demand fluctuations.
architecture: Historical Sales Ingestion -> Data Cleaning & Outlier Imputation -> Temporal & Autoregressive Feature Engineering -> Train/Test Split (Time-Ordered) -> XGBoost Regressor Hyperparameter Tuning -> Residual Diagnostics & Accuracy Evaluation -> Interactive Prediction UI.
results: Achieved R² = 0.92 on a held-out test set (training R² = 0.97).
challenges: Avoiding data leakage across temporal splits while engineering rolling statistical aggregates. Enforced strict causal lag windows calculated solely on historical observations.

title: ArticleSift: LLM News Question-Answering
summary: A news question-answering and summarization app that retrieves current reporting with Google Custom Search and adds audio narration and multilingual translation.
problem: Answering questions about current events requires finding relevant, up-to-date news and making the information accessible in different languages and formats.
solution: Built a question-answering and summarization app that retrieves live news using Google Custom Search and uses LLaMA 3.1 to analyze the results. The app includes five API endpoints, audio narration, and translation into English, Urdu, Spanish, and French.
architecture: Question -> Google Custom Search API retrieval -> LLaMA 3.1 analysis and response -> Streamlit interface, with optional gTTS narration and multilingual translation.
results: The app supports live-news question answering and summarization, five API endpoints, audio narration, and four-language translation.
challenges: Working with current news requires retrieving relevant reporting for each query and presenting the response in accessible formats.
